symbols.name: \(\delta\)
symbols.role: oracle-regime lower bound for nonclose scores

symbols.name: d
symbols.role: dimension of each primitive micro observation

symbols.name: p
symbols.role: dimension of the stacked score-effect vector

symbols.name: \(n_r\)
symbols.def: number of micro units sampled from group \(r\)

symbols.name: \(Y_{ri}(a)\)
symbols.def: post-period outcome for unit \(i\) in group \(r\) under group-treatment status \(a\)

symbols.name: \(Y_{ri}^{\mathrm{pre}}\)
symbols.def: the prespecified baseline outcome for unit \(i\) in group \(r\), measured before group treatment

symbols.name: \(G_{ri}\)
symbols.def: the prespecified vector of baseline outcomes, baseline outcome slopes, and baseline case-mix summaries used to predict untreated post-period changes for unit \(i\) in group \(r\)

symbols.name: \(W_{ri}\)
symbols.def: the fixed-dimensional observable vector containing \(Y_{ri}^{\mathrm{pre}}\), \(G_{ri}\), \(Y_{ri}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and prespecified covariates for unit \(i\) in group \(r\)

symbols.name: \(P_{r,n}\)
symbols.def: the group \(r\), index \(n\) probability law of the observable vector \(W_{ri}\)

symbols.name: \(P_{r,n}^{\star}\)
symbols.def: a joint law of \(W_{ri}\), \(Y_{ri}(0)\), and \(Y_{ri}(1)\) whose \(W_{ri}\)-marginal is \(P_{r,n}\)

symbols.name: \(\mathbb P_n\)
symbols.def: \(\mathbb P_n=\bigotimes_{r\in\mathcal R}P_{r,n}^{\otimes n_r}\) on the observed sample \(\{W_{ri}:r\in\mathcal R,1\le i\le n_r\}\)

symbols.name: \(\omega_{jr}\)
symbols.def: for each \(j\in\mathcal J\), \(\omega_{jr}=0\) when \(r\in\mathcal T\) and \(\sum_{r\in\mathcal R\setminus\mathcal T}\omega_{jr}=1\)

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: the prespecified matrix mapping primitive group means to the \(J\) treated-minus-donor predictor-score and observed-change blocks defined below

symbols.name: \(s_{j,n}\)
symbols.def: \(s_{j,n}=\sum_{r\in\mathcal T}\pi_rg_{r,n}-\sum_{r\in\mathcal R\setminus\mathcal T}\omega_{jr}g_{r,n}\), which is the first \(q\) coordinates of \(E_j\theta_n\)

symbols.name: \(b_{j,n}\)
symbols.def: \(b_{j,n}=\sum_{r\in\mathcal T}\pi_r\mathbb E_{P_{r,n}}[Y_{ri}^{\mathrm{obs}}-Y_{ri}^{\mathrm{pre}}]-\sum_{r\in\mathcal R\setminus\mathcal T}\omega_{jr}\mathbb E_{P_{r,n}}[Y_{ri}^{\mathrm{obs}}-Y_{ri}^{\mathrm{pre}}]\), the last coordinate of \(E_j\theta_n\)

symbols.name: \(\tau_n\)
symbols.type: average treatment effect on the treated

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak M(\delta)\)
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M(\delta)=\{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M:\inf_{n\ge1}\min_{j\in\mathcal J\setminus\mathcal C_n}\|s_{j,n}\|_2\ge\delta\}\), with the minimum over an empty set equal to \(+\infty\)

symbols.name: \(c_{1-\alpha}(\Omega)\)
symbols.def: the \(1-\alpha\) quantile of \(\max_{j\in\mathcal J}\|(E_j\Omega E_j^{\top})^{-1/2}E_jZ\|_2\) for \(Z\sim N(0,\Omega)\)

symbols.name: \(I_{j,n}(\alpha)\)
symbols.role: profile of the joint Wald ellipsoid under label \(j\)

symbols.name: \(C_n^{\mathrm{proj}}(\alpha)\)
symbols.role: convex hull of all nonempty labelwise profiles

symbols.name: \(\mathcal D_n\)
symbols.def: the prespecified report of score confidence regions, exact-calibration residuals, held-out pre-period placebo changes, omitted-predictor balance, donor leverage, and effective sample sizes at index \(n\)

symbols.name: \(\mathcal H_H\)
symbols.role: bounded union of exact-zero score faces

symbols.name: \(L_{\mathrm{sw}}\)
symbols.def: under the declared \(J=2\), \(q=1\) specialization, \(L_{\mathrm{sw}}\) selects and standardizes the two scalar score coordinates of \(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}\)

symbols.name: \(L_{\perp}\)
symbols.def: under the declared \(J=2\), \(q=1\) specialization, \(L_{\perp}\) selects the remaining coordinates of \(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}\)

symbols.name: \(U^{\mathrm{sw}}\)
symbols.def: \(U^{\mathrm{sw}}=L_{\perp}Z^{\mathrm{pan}}\), constrained in the embedded panel submodel to be independent of \(Z^{\mathrm{sw}}\) and to have the same distribution under \(\ell=0\) and \(\ell=1\)

symbols.name: \(C^{\mathrm{NP}}_{c,\Delta,\alpha}\)
symbols.role: attaining rule in the two-point donor-switch experiment

symbols.name: \(\mathcal K\)
symbols.def: a fixed compact subset of \(\mathcal H_H\times\{\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p:\underline\omega I_p\preceq\Omega\preceq\overline\omega I_p\}\)

symbols.name: \(\mathbb P_{n,\eta}\)
symbols.def: the member at index \(n\) and local parameter \(\eta\) of a dominated QMD subfamily of the product laws \(\mathbb P_n\)

symbols.name: \(\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{mean}}\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{mean}}=\{\mathcal L_{\mathbb P_{n,\eta}}(((\sqrt n\,\widehat s_{j,n})_{j\in\mathcal J},(\widehat b_{j,n})_{j\in\mathcal J})):\eta\in\mathcal K\}\)

assumptions.condition: For every \(n\ge1\), \(r\in\mathcal R\), and \(1\le i\le n_r\), \(Y_{ri}^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_{ri}(1)\) \(P_{r,n}^{\star}\)-almost surely when \(r\in\mathcal T\) and \(Y_{ri}^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_{ri}(0)\) \(P_{r,n}^{\star}\)-almost surely when \(r\in\mathcal R\setminus\mathcal T\).

standard.name: SUTVA consistency for observed treatment histories
uniform nonsingularity of the Gaussian information matrix

novel.justification: The condition defines an abstract conditional design regime and is not asserted for the historical CMS workflow. It is credible in designs that algebraically calibrate a donor stack ex ante to known administrative population totals for every prespecified trend predictor. Score intervals and calibration residuals may falsify this regime, but ranked sample near-balance cannot establish it.

assumptions.condition: For every \(n\ge1\) and \(r\in\mathcal R\), \(\mathbb E_{P_{r,n}^{\star}}[Y_{ri}(0)-Y_{ri}^{\mathrm{pre}}\mid G_{ri}]=\kappa_n+\beta_n^{\top}G_{ri}\) \(P_{r,n}^{\star}\)-almost surely.

novel.justification: This shared-slope conditional-mean model is realistic when baseline levels, pre-period slopes, and case mix exhaust systematic cross-state differences in untreated changes, while individual residual heterogeneity remains unrestricted. Its implications can be challenged using held-out pre-period changes, omitted-predictor balance, and slope-stability checks.

This bounded local union records a finite menu with at least one exact donor and permits several exact donors. Such configurations arise when administratively eligible donor states share calibrated baseline moments while other candidates differ on the sampling-error scale.

The restriction is the limit-experiment form of exact-donor causal coherence. It allows arbitrary disagreement away from the active face and only equates effects for donors whose prespecified validity scores are exactly zero.

definitions.name: Exact-close triangular-array class \(\mathfrak M\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M=\{\mathbf P=(\mathbb P_n)_{n\ge1}:\mathbb P_n=\bigotimes_{r\in\mathcal R}P_{r,n}^{\otimes n_r}\text{ for every }n\ge1,\text{ and there exists a full array }(P_{r,n}^{\star})_{r\in\mathcal R,n\ge1}\text{ for which ass:consistency, ass:stable-fractions, ass:uniform-fourth-moment, ass:covariance-regularity, ass:nonempty-close-set, and ass:additive-untreated-change hold}\}\).

definitions.name: Stacked score-effect estimator
definitions.construction: Compute each \(\widehat\mu_{r,n}=n_r^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_r}W_{ri}\), stack these vectors as \(\widehat\mu_n\), and set \(\widehat\theta_n=A\widehat\mu_n\).

definitions.name: Shared-group covariance estimator and spectral clipping
definitions.construction: Compute the centered within-group covariances \(\widehat\Sigma_{r,n}\), set \(\widehat\Omega_n=A\operatorname{diag}_{r\in\mathcal R}((n/n_r)\widehat\Sigma_{r,n})A^{\top}\), symmetrize it, and clip every eigenvalue to \([\underline\omega/2,2\overline\omega]\) to obtain \(\widetilde\Omega_n\).

definitions.name: Labelwise joint-Wald profiles
definitions.construction: Partition \(E_j\widetilde\Omega_nE_j^{\top}\) as \(\begin{pmatrix}\widehat V_{j,n}&\widehat u_{j,n}\\\widehat u_{j,n}^{\top}&\widehat v_{j,n}\end{pmatrix}\), compute \(\widehat\gamma_{j,n}=\widehat V_{j,n}^{-1}\widehat u_{j,n}\), \(\widehat\sigma_{j,n}^2=\widehat v_{j,n}-\widehat u_{j,n}^{\top}\widehat V_{j,n}^{-1}\widehat u_{j,n}\), \(Q_{j,n}=n\widehat s_{j,n}^{\top}\widehat V_{j,n}^{-1}\widehat s_{j,n}\), and \(\widehat c_n=c_{1-\alpha}(\widetilde\Omega_n)\). If \(Q_{j,n}\le\widehat c_n^2\), set \(I_{j,n}(\alpha)=[\widehat b_{j,n}-\widehat\gamma_{j,n}^{\top}\widehat s_{j,n}\;\pm\;n^{-1/2}\widehat\sigma_{j,n}(\widehat c_n^2-Q_{j,n})^{1/2}]\); otherwise set \(I_{j,n}(\alpha)=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Maximum-critical labelwise hull
definitions.construction: \(C_n^{\mathrm{proj}}(\alpha)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{j\in\mathcal J}I_{j,n}(\alpha))\), with the convex hull of the empty set defined as the empty set.

definitions.name: Observable exact-close diagnostic protocol
definitions.construction: Construct \(\mathcal D_n\) by reporting, for every \(j\in\mathcal J\), the joint confidence region for \(s_{j,n}\), the numerical calibration residual \(\widehat s_{j,n}\), any documented ex ante algebraic calibration to known administrative population totals, held-out pre-period change residuals not included in \(G_{ri}\), balance for prespecified omitted-risk summaries, the maximum donor weight \(\max_{r\in\mathcal R}\omega_{jr}\), and group effective sample sizes. Absence of documented population-total calibration is reported rather than replaced by ranked sample near-balance.

definitions.name: Bounded Gaussian donor-face space \(\mathcal H_H\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal H_H=\{(h,b)\in(\mathbb R^q)^J\times\mathbb R^J:\min_{j\in\mathcal J}\|h_j\|_2=0,\ \max_{j\in\mathcal J}\|h_j\|_2\le H,\ h_j=h_k=0\Rightarrow b_j=b_k\}\).

definitions.name: Gaussian honest expected-diameter frontier
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)=\inf_K\sup_{(h,b)\in\mathcal H_H}\mathbb E_{h,b,\Omega}[\operatorname{diam}(K(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}))]\), where the infimum is over measurable confidence kernels \(K:\mathbb R^p\rightsquigarrow2^{\mathbb R}\) satisfying \(\inf_{(h,b)\in\mathcal H_H}\Pr_{h,b,\Omega}\{\tau(h,b)\in K(Z^{\mathrm{pan}})\}\ge1-\alpha\).

definitions.name: Two-donor switch experiment
definitions.construction: Observe the explicitly two-dimensional score vector \(Z^{\mathrm{sw}}\). Under state \(\ell=0\), \(Z^{\mathrm{sw}}\sim N((0,c)^{\top},I_2)\) and the ATT is \(0\); under state \(\ell=1\), \(Z^{\mathrm{sw}}\sim N((c,0)^{\top},I_2)\) and the ATT is \(\Delta\). The maps \(L_{\mathrm{sw}}\) and \(L_{\perp}\) embed the experiment in \(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}\) when \(J=2\), \(q=1\), \(b=(0,\Delta)^{\top}\), \(L_{\mathrm{sw}}\Omega L_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\top}=I_2\), and \(U^{\mathrm{sw}}\) is independent of \(Z^{\mathrm{sw}}\) with a state-invariant law.

definitions.name: Two-score Gaussian maximum benchmark
definitions.construction: For \(z=(z_1,z_2)^{\top}\in\mathbb R^2\), set \(K_{\max,\alpha,\Delta}(z)=\operatorname{conv}(\{t\in\{0\}:|z_1|\le k_{\alpha}\}\cup\{t\in\{\Delta\}:|z_2|\le k_{\alpha}\})\), where \(k_{\alpha}\) is determined by \((2\Phi(k_{\alpha})-1)^2=1-\alpha\).

definitions.name: Finite-face decision-dual handle
definitions.construction: Represent a confidence kernel by its donor-face acceptance regions; impose the coverage constraints face by face; then apply Bayes--minimax duality and Gaussian likelihood-ratio ordering to optimize their overlap, allowing randomized boundary rules when several zero-score faces meet.

definitions.name: Restricted QMD reduced-experiment transfer handle
definitions.construction: Restrict the product laws to the dominated QMD family \(\{\mathbb P_{n,\eta}:\eta\in\mathcal K\}\), use the common parameter map \(\psi_n(\eta)=((\sqrt n\,s_{j,n})_{j\in\mathcal J},(b_{j,n})_{j\in\mathcal J},\Omega_n)\), and compare only the reduced experiment \(\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{mean}}\) with its Gaussian counterpart. Construct two-sided Markov kernels by QMD/LAN likelihood-ratio approximation and Nussbaum-style smoothing after proving \(\sup_{\eta\in\mathcal K}\|\psi_n(\eta)-\eta\|\to0\). Treat tail control separately by requiring uniform integrability of the candidate diameter losses, for example through a uniform moment bound of order strictly greater than one.

statements.statement: For every triangular array \(\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M\), every compatible causal extension array \((P_{r,n}^{\star})_{r\in\mathcal R,n\ge1}\) satisfying ass:consistency and ass:additive-untreated-change, every \(n\ge1\), and every \(j\in\mathcal J\), iterated expectations and the prespecified predictor-score construction imply \(b_{j,n}-\tau_n=\beta_n^{\top}s_{j,n}\). Therefore every \(j\in\mathcal C_n\) satisfies \(b_{j,n}=\tau_n\), and all such compatible extensions and all labels on a multiple-close-donor face identify the same ATT.
statements.justification: This lemma derives the load-bearing causal coherence from observable score content and an explicit untreated-change law instead of assuming the identifying conclusion.
statements.gap: Exact pre-balance is often invoked as a design heuristic; the stated identity records the precise additive transport restriction under which it identifies every close-label contrast as the same ATT.
statements.consumer: It defines a falsifiable score-content requirement for a new comparison-state analysis; it does not validate the historical CMS estimates from ranked near-balance.

statements.statement: As \(n\to\infty\), \(\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M}d_{\mathrm{Pr}}(\mathcal L_{\mathbb P_n}(\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n)),N(0,\Omega_n))\to0\) and \(\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M}\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_n}[\min\{1,\|\widehat\Omega_n-\Omega_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\}]\to0\). The formula for \(\Omega_n\) retains every covariance induced by a treated group or control group reused across donor labels.
statements.justification: This lemma replaces a many-control reference distribution by within-group micro-sample Gaussianity while preserving shared-control dependence.
statements.gap: Conley and Taber and Ferman and Pinto obtain few-treated inference from many control groups; the present covariance law uses fixed labels and growing micro samples within each primitive group.
statements.consumer: It supplies an estimable joint law for CMS comparisons that reuse treated populations and candidate comparison states across outcomes.

statements.statement: As \(n\to\infty\), \(\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M}\Pr_{\mathbb P_n}\{\widetilde\Omega_n\ne\widehat\Omega_n\}\to0\) and \(\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M}\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_n}[\min\{1,\|\widetilde\Omega_n-\Omega_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\}]\to0\). On every sample, \(\underline\omega/2\le\lambda_{\min}(\widetilde\Omega_n)\le\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde\Omega_n)\le2\overline\omega\); hence every label-block inverse, regression coefficient, Schur-complement residual variance, and Gaussian critical value used by the feasible hull is defined.
statements.justification: Spectral clipping makes the feasible confidence set a total procedure on every finite sample without changing its uniform first-order behavior.
statements.gap: Covariance-consistency arguments usually proceed on a high-probability nonsingularity event; this lemma exposes and controls the fallback needed by the donor-face procedure.
statements.consumer: Implementations can return a defined interval even for small or collinear within-group samples while retaining the stated asymptotic guarantees.

statements.statement: For every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the spectrally clipped feasible construction satisfies \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M}\Pr_{\mathbb P_n}\{\tau_n\in C_n^{\mathrm{proj}}(\alpha)\}\ge1-\alpha\). The infimum ranges over the full exact-close triangular-array class, including fixed and \(n^{-1/2}\)-local score separations, every covariance array satisfying the eigenvalue bounds, unequal stable group sizes, and every multiple-close-donor face.
statements.justification: The result gives a feasible honest baseline that propagates score uncertainty, post-outcome uncertainty, and dependence across labels in one inversion.
statements.gap: Berk et al. establish generic simultaneous post-selection coverage, while Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey study winner selection; neither profiles a causal target defined by exact zero-score donor faces.
statements.consumer: CMS evaluators can report an ATT interval that remains valid when two or three comparison states are retained or replaced because of claims availability.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(\delta>0\), \(\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M(\delta)}\Pr_{\mathbb P_n}\{\exists j\in\mathcal J\setminus\mathcal C_n:I_{j,n}(\alpha)\ne\varnothing\}\to0\), and \(\lim_{\xi\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M(\delta)}\Pr_{\mathbb P_n}\{\sqrt n\operatorname{diam}(C_n^{\mathrm{proj}}(\alpha))>\xi\}=0\).
statements.justification: Honesty near label collisions is useful only if the method recovers ordinary root-sample precision when donors are separated.
statements.gap: Projection methods are known to be conservative, but the exact fixed-separation recovery statement for zero-score donor labels is not supplied by the general post-selection literature.
statements.consumer: Applications with one clearly matching comparison state pay no first-order diameter penalty for guarding against weak separation.

statements.statement: In the explicitly two-dimensional observation experiment \(Z^{\mathrm{sw}}\), the minimum over all confidence kernels \(K:\mathbb R^2\rightsquigarrow2^{\{0,\Delta\}}\) satisfying \(\min_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}\Pr_{\ell}\{\ell\Delta\in K(Z^{\mathrm{sw}})\}\ge1-\alpha\) of \(\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{\ell}[\operatorname{diam}(K(Z^{\mathrm{sw}}))]\) is \(r_2(c,\Delta,\alpha)=\Delta[\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\sqrt2c)-\alpha]_+\). The rule \(C^{\mathrm{NP}}_{c,\Delta,\alpha}\) attains this value, including the zero-overlap regime. Under the \(J=2\), \(q=1\) panel submodel with \(b=(0,\Delta)^{\top}\), \(L_{\mathrm{sw}}\Omega L_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\top}=I_2\), and state-invariant independent \(U^{\mathrm{sw}}\), the full observation \(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}\) is equivalent to the switch experiment augmented by an ancillary variable, so the same minimax value and rule apply.
statements.justification: The closed form identifies the exact price of honest adaptation at the smallest nontrivial donor collision and supplies the base case for the general dual program.
statements.gap: Evans, Hansen, and Stark give a general Bayes--minimax confidence-set duality, and Cai and Low give modulus lower bounds; neither solves this discontinuous two-face causal target.
statements.consumer: The formula is an exact calibration benchmark for any simultaneous or conditional donor-selection interval.

statements.statement: In the independent two-score switch experiment, the explicitly defined Gaussian donor-face benchmark \(K_{\max,\alpha,\Delta}\) satisfies \(\min_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}\Pr_{\ell}\{\ell\Delta\in K_{\max,\alpha,\Delta}(Z^{\mathrm{sw}})\}\ge1-\alpha\). Its worst-state expected diameter is \(r_{\max}(c,\Delta,\alpha)=\Delta(2\Phi(k_{\alpha})-1)[\Phi(k_{\alpha}-c)-\Phi(-k_{\alpha}-c)]\), where \((2\Phi(k_{\alpha})-1)^2=1-\alpha\). At \(\alpha=0.05\), \(c=1\), and \(\Delta=0.4\), \(r_2=0.2165\) whereas \(r_{\max}=0.3475\), so the Gaussian maximum benchmark is not minimax. Under the state-invariant independent \(U^{\mathrm{sw}}\) factorization in def:two-donor-switch, the same benchmark and risk embed in the full panel Gaussian observation.
statements.justification: The proposition executes the early kill test with a fully specified score-only confidence kernel and rules out its minimax optimality.
statements.gap: Berk et al. emphasize the insurance cost of simultaneity qualitatively; this calculation gives the exact cost in the donor-switch experiment.
statements.consumer: It tells method developers how much expected diameter remains available to a face-adaptive replacement.

statements.statement: For every declared score dimension \(q\in\mathbb N\), when \(J=1\), \(C_n^{\mathrm{proj}}(\alpha)\) equals the profile of the ordinary \(q+1\)-dimensional Gaussian Wald ellipsoid under the restriction \(s_{1,n}=0\).
statements.justification: This reduction verifies that the construction nests standard inference when label ambiguity disappears.
statements.gap: The reduction is a required coherence check rather than a claimed departure from standard Wald theory.
statements.consumer: Software can test the implementation against ordinary one-label regression output.

statements.statement: Characterize \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)\) by a finite-dimensional primal--dual program, determine a least-favorable distribution over donor faces, and construct an attaining confidence kernel for arbitrary fixed \(J\), arbitrary positive definite \(\Omega\), and multiple-zero-label faces. Determine exactly when the optimized rule strictly improves on \(C_n^{\mathrm{proj}}(\alpha)\) after passage to the Gaussian experiment.
statements.justification: This is the paper's central open content: an exact honest-diameter frontier on the stratified donor-face experiment.
statements.gap: Restricted-Gaussian confidence-set duality does not cover a target map that changes with the active zero-coordinate face, and post-selection methods do not optimize worst-face expected diameter.
statements.consumer: A solution yields the shortest defensible ATT interval for every fixed donor menu and supplies a reusable decision primitive for tie and moment-selection problems.

statements.statement: For the dominated QMD subfamily \(\{\mathbb P_{n,\eta}:\eta\in\mathcal K\}\), determine primitive regularity under which the reduced sample-mean experiment \(\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{mean}}\) is uniformly asymptotically equivalent, in Le Cam deficiency, to a Gaussian donor-face experiment indexed by the same \(\eta=(h,b,\Omega)\). Require the common map \(\psi_n\) to satisfy \(\sup_{\eta\in\mathcal K}\|\psi_n(\eta)-\eta\|\to0\), which separately entails uniform convergence of the local score means, \((b_{j,n})_{j\in\mathcal J}\), and \(\Omega_n\) on the compact parameter set. Establish two-sided kernel approximation only for this restricted or reduced experiment, and prove expected-diameter risk transfer under a separate uniform-integrability condition on the candidate confidence kernels, including multiple-zero-label faces.
statements.justification: A common parameter map and restricted regular family are necessary before Gaussian optimality can be transferred through the discontinuous active-face target map.
statements.gap: Nussbaum proves global deficiency equivalence only under strong domination, smoothness, positivity, compactness, and bounded-loss structure; fourth moments for arbitrary group laws do not supply those ingredients or uniform integrability for diameter loss.
statements.consumer: A solution identifies the additional design and tail conditions under which a Gaussian face-optimal rule has a defensible reduced-micro-panel analogue.

sampling_model.design: Fixed finite treated groups and prespecified donor stacks. Each donor stack has known comparison-group weights, and its score is exactly the treated-minus-donor contrast in the baseline levels, pre-period slopes, and case-mix summaries collected in \(G_{ri}\).
sampling_model.units: At each \(n\), the observable sample has the product joint law \(\mathbb P_n=\bigotimes_{r\in\mathcal R}P_{r,n}^{\otimes n_r}\); the model is the full triangular array \(\mathbf P=(\mathbb P_n)_{n\ge1}\).
sampling_model.treatment: A fixed realized group-level treatment history. Consistency and the shared-slope additive untreated-change model give the causal interpretation, conditional on the score containing every systematic untreated-trend predictor.
sampling_model.overlap: Every primitive group has a limiting sample fraction bounded away from zero; no treatment-propensity overlap condition is used.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Group means and within-group covariance matrices are estimated directly; the known contrast matrix propagates shared treated and reused-control covariance. The symmetric covariance estimator is spectrally clipped to \([\underline\omega/2,2\overline\omega]\), so all feasible inverses and critical values are defined. The diagnostic report records score uncertainty, any documented ex ante population-total calibration, held-out placebo trends, omitted-predictor balance, donor leverage, and effective sample sizes.

estimand_functional: \(C_n^{\mathrm{proj}}(\alpha)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{j\in\mathcal J}I_{j,n}(\alpha))\), with the optimal weak-separation benchmark \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Projection intervals are universally valid after noisy winner selection but can be substantially longer than selection-tailored intervals.
Bayes--minimax duality characterizes confidence sets minimizing worst-case expected measure for restricted Gaussian location parameters.
Simultaneous inference yields universal validity after arbitrary model selection at a possible precision cost.
Subsequence arguments give GMM inference uniform over unidentified, weak, semi-strong, and strong regimes.
Conditional Gaussian inference controls size uniformly without imposing identification-strength restrictions.
Few-treated-group difference-in-differences inference accommodates heteroskedasticity induced by unequal group sizes using many controls.
Cross-fitted bias correction and self-normalization yield average synthetic-control-effect inference under time-series asymptotics.
Theorem 1.1 establishes global Le Cam equivalence between i.i.d. density estimation and Gaussian white noise over densities in a Hölder ball with exponent above one half and bounded away from zero.

tldr: A small fixed menu of prespecified donor stacks creates a nonregular inference problem when validity is exact equality of a noisy score containing baseline levels, pre-period slopes, and case mix. Under an almost-sure shared-slope model for untreated post-minus-pre changes, iterated expectations make exact score equality imply the same ATT for every close donor. Spectral clipping totalizes the feasible joint Gaussian profiles, which are uniformly honest on this conditional triangular-array class and root-sample narrow under fixed separation. An explicitly two-dimensional donor-switch experiment has an exact likelihood-ratio minimax rule, reducing worst-case expected diameter from \(0.3475\) for a defined Gaussian maximum benchmark to \(0.2165\). The general finite-face frontier and transfer from a restricted QMD reduced-mean experiment remain open. Ranked near-balance does not validate the historical CMS estimates.

project_justification.gap: Existing few-treated panel methods use many untreated groups, synthetic-control methods use long time series, and generic post-selection methods do not optimize confidence-set diameter for a target whose label is defined by an exact zero score.
project_justification.niche: The CMS comparison-state workflow has finitely many candidate labels, many beneficiaries within each state, unequal sample sizes, reused groups, and uncertainty about which comparisons satisfy a prespecified exact transport score. Its causal interpretation requires both an exact population equality and a transparent model connecting the score to untreated changes; ranked sample balance supplies neither.
project_justification.fill: The project derives exact-close transport by iterated expectations under an almost-sure shared-slope untreated-change model, supplies falsifying calibration and placebo diagnostics, proves conditional uniform validity and fixed-separation oracle behavior for a spectrally clipped joint inversion, solves the embedded two-donor honest-diameter problem exactly, and leaves general face-adaptive minimaxity and restricted QMD reduced-experiment transfer as explicit open questions.

related_work: RTI International documents a CMS comparison-state workflow based on ranked baseline distance, two or three retained states, claims-driven substitutions, and person-level weighting. The reviewed methods source does not document ex ante algebraic calibration to known administrative population totals. Observed ranked near-balance therefore does not prove exact equality, and the exact-face theorem does not validate the historical CMS estimates; the workflow is only a motivating, falsifiable use case. Conley and Taber and Ferman and Pinto treat few policy-changing groups, but their reference distribution comes from many controls rather than many micro observations inside fixed labels. Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu's JPE article, \emph{Debiasing and t-Tests for Synthetic Control Inference on Average Causal Effects}, develops cross-fitted debiasing and self-normalized t-tests for synthetic-control average causal effects, not exact donor-face uncertainty. Berk et al. justify universal post-selection coverage through simultaneity. Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey show why projection is honest but potentially imprecise after noisy option selection. Evans, Hansen, and Stark provide the acceptance-region Bayes--minimax template that informs the stratified target-map problem. Andrews and Cheng and Andrews and Mikusheva supply weak-identification asymptotics but not deficiency or expected-diameter risk transfer on donor faces. Nussbaum's Theorem 1.1 and Section 2 establish full deficiency equivalence through domination, Hölder smoothness above one half, positivity, compact parameter control, and explicit likelihood-process approximation; these stronger ingredients explain why fourth moments alone cannot support an unrestricted raw-data equivalence claim here. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato justify covariance-estimated Gaussian maxima, which support the feasible benchmark rather than its decision-theoretic optimality.
technical_internal_limitation: The explicit Gaussian maximum benchmark fails the early optimality test. In the two-donor identity-covariance switch with \(c=1\), \(\Delta=0.4\), and \(\alpha=0.05\), its worst expected diameter is \(0.3475\), while the exact Neyman--Pearson value is \(0.2165\); the elementary total-variation bound \(0.1518\) is not sharp. General optimized inversion remains open, and transfer beyond a restricted QMD or reduced-sample-mean experiment is not claimed.
honest_scope: Uniform coverage and fixed-separation root-sample diameter are theorem targets only over the exact-close triangular-array class satisfying the almost-sure shared-slope additive untreated-change model, with every feasible inverse and critical value computed from the spectrally clipped covariance matrix. Diagnostics can reveal failures of calibration, placebo fit, omitted-predictor balance, or donor support, but ranked empirical near-balance does not prove exact population equality or causal transport. No reviewed source documents ex ante CMS algebraic calibration to known administrative population totals, so the exact-face results do not validate the historical CMS estimates. The exact embedded two-donor minimax formula and the explicit Gaussian maximum benchmark are theorem targets. General multiple-face minimax optimality and transfer from a restricted QMD reduced experiment under separate uniform-integrability conditions are open-ended questions; unrestricted raw-data Le Cam equivalence and maximum-critical optimality are not claimed.

literature_map.settled: Comparison-state construction and inference with alternative replication schemes are documented.
literature_map.open_boundary: Fixed donor labels with within-label micro replication and joint validity-score uncertainty are not covered.

literature_map.settled: Simultaneous, conditional, and hybrid inference can correct noisy selection of conventional targets.
literature_map.open_boundary: The target here is indexed by exact zero-coordinate faces and must agree on face intersections.

literature_map.settled: Acceptance-region duality and modulus arguments deliver minimax expected-measure bounds in regular restricted Gaussian problems.
literature_map.open_boundary: No located theorem solves the donor-face target map or its multiple-face intersections.

literature_map.settled: Uniform size across drifting identification regimes can be organized through Gaussian limits, while Nussbaum proves global deficiency equivalence under strong domination, smoothness, positivity, and compactness conditions.
literature_map.open_boundary: Two-sided equivalence is posed only for a restricted QMD reduced-mean family with a common parameter map; unbounded diameter-risk transfer additionally requires separate uniform-integrability control.

literature_map.settled: Equivalence tests, pretest distortions, sensitivity regions, and inference after set selection are available separately.
literature_map.open_boundary: Their combination would define a different partial-identification angle, not subsume the exact-close frontier.

novelty_justification.precise_gap: The closest selection paper studies a winner among Gaussian estimates, while the closest minimax paper studies confidence sets for a fixed restricted location parameter. Neither has a causal target that is selected by which score coordinate is exactly zero and constrained to agree only where zero-coordinate faces intersect.
novelty_justification.strict_delta: The two-donor theorem gives a closed-form minimax risk and an attaining likelihood-ratio rule. The calibrated maximum-critical risk is \(0.3475\), strictly above the exact value \(0.2165\); thus the proposed decision object is not a relabeling of simultaneous projection.
novelty_justification.search_conclusion: Direct target--method searches across Gaussian union models, post-selection confidence sets, weak identification, and honest expected length found no closer paper that states or subsumes the donor-face kernel.
